newsitem.title: USA: VF, Maidenform call off merger talks.
newsitem.headline: VF, Maidenform call off merger talks.

text.p: Jeans and lingerie maker VF Corp. and Maidenform Worldwide Inc., manufacturer of women's intimate apparel, said Thursday they called off their merger talks.
The companies said they "have mutually agreed to terminate their discussions concerning the previously announced proposed purchase of all of the outstanding common stock of Maidenform."
No reason was given for the decision.

In late March, VF, the No. 3 maker of women's lingerie, with the Vanity Fair and Vasarette brands, announced plans to buy Maidenform, whose products include the Maidenform, Oscar de la Renta, Lilyette, Flexees, Subtract and Self Expression labels, for undisclosed terms.
At that time, both companies stressed that they had signed a letter of intent, but said more financial and legal reviews were needed before a definitive agreement would be reached.
Privately held Maidenform, which earlier this year announced it would consider options to ensure the company's future growth, said it will now pursue other opportunities.

"We intend to resume immediately previous discussions concerning other opportunities for the company. I am confident in the potential of the Maidenform business and look forward to new discussions to help secure our long-term success," said Chairman Elizabeth Coleman.
VF said the failed talks will have little impact on its positive outlook for the intimate apparel business.
"It's one of the categories we've targeted for growth. This doesn't change our strategy one way or the other," VF spokeswoman Cindy Knoebel said.

The deal would have expanded the role of Wyomissing, Pa.-based VF in the booming market for body-slimming undergarments. Currently, VF has about 11 percent of the $9.8 billion intimate apparel industry and Maidenform holds about a 10 percent share.
VF also owns Lee and Wrangler jeans, Healthtex, JanSport and Jantzen lines. VF's stock was up 37.5 cents to at $67.875 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
New York-based Maidenform also owns 92 percent of the outstanding stock of NCC Industries Inc., which makes intimate apparel in larger sizes.
